comments.note: ThumbnailsView.axaml.cs OnThumbnailsCollectionChanged does not handle NotifyCollectionChangedAction.Reset. When the ViewModel's Load command calls Thumbnails.Clear() (which fires a Reset event with OldItems=null), the View's per-item PropertyChanged subscriptions to the old disposed items are not cleaned up. This creates a lightweight but technically incorrect memory hold: disposed ThumbnailItemViewModel instances remain referenced by the View's event subscription until DataContext is changed. In practice the disposed items never fire PropertyChanged again, so there is no crash risk, but across repeated load cycles the View accumulates stale delegate references. Fix: add a Reset branch in OnThumbnailsCollectionChanged that unsubscribes all currently tracked items before the new items are added.

The 'Delete Selected' toolbar button carries both IsEnabled="{Binding HasSelection}" and Command="{Binding DeleteSelectedCommand}" where CanDeleteSelected() already checks HasSelection && !IsBusy. The explicit IsEnabled binding is redundant — the command's CanExecute is the authoritative disabled-state signal for this button. Removing the IsEnabled binding would simplify the XAML and give full ownership to the command; the current dual-ownership creates a misleading split where the binding covers HasSelection but silently ignores the IsBusy guard (Avalonia still applies CanExecute=false when IsBusy=true, so no behavioral bug exists). Low-priority cosmetic cleanup.
